docs.title: Scheme gnuplot-dataframe Library
docs.text:
Plot dataframes with gnuplot from Chez Scheme.

The API is loosely modeled on base R plotting: one procedure per plot type, column names for the data, and options for labels, legends, and output. Like ggplot2, a 'group column splits the data into colored series with a legend, layers can be combined on the same axes, and a 'facet column splits a plot into panels.

GitHub · dataframe · gnuplot-pipe

docs.title: Quick Example
docs.text:
(import (dataframe)
        (gnuplot-dataframe))

(define temps
  (make-df* (month 1 2 3 4 1 2 3 4)
            (city "Davis" "Davis" "Davis" "Davis"
                  "Chicago" "Chicago" "Chicago" "Chicago")
            (temp 8 10 13 15 -5 -3 3 9)))

;; opens a gnuplot window
(plot-lines temps 'month 'temp 'group 'city 'points #t)

;; writes a file instead
(plot-lines temps 'month 'temp 'group 'city 'points #t
            'ylabel "Temperature (°C)"
            'output "temps.png")

docs.title: Gallery
docs.text: The code for these plots is in examples/examples.ss.

docs.title: API Overview
docs.text: Section Procedures Plots plot-points, plot-lines, plot-bars, plot-histogram, plot-boxplot Options 'group, 'title, 'key, 'output, … Layers plot-layers, layer-points, layer-lines, layer-bars, layer-histogram, layer-boxplot Facets 'facet, 'facet-columns, 'facet-scales gnuplot Scripts plot-dry-run, 'commands

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text: gnuplot 5.2.6 or later. Tested with gnuplot 6.0 and Chez Scheme 10.3.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Clone this repository and its dependencies, dataframe and gnuplot-pipe:

$ git clone https://github.com/hinkelman/gnuplot-dataframe
$ git clone https://github.com/hinkelman/dataframe
$ git clone https://github.com/hinkelman/gnuplot-pipe

Then add the three directories to Chez Scheme's library path, e.g., in your shell profile:

$ export CHEZSCHEMELIBDIRS="/path/to/gnuplot-dataframe:/path/to/dataframe:/path/to/gnuplot-pipe:$CHEZSCHEMELIBDIRS"

Those libraries have dependencies of their own, which also need to be on the library path: gnuplot-pipe uses SRFI 1 and SRFI 13 (e.g., from chez-srfi), and dataframe uses (slib format).

docs.title: Import
docs.text:
(import (dataframe)
        (gnuplot-dataframe))

docs.title: Windows and files
docs.text:
By default, each plot opens in a new gnuplot window. To write a file instead, pass 'output with a file name ending in .png, .svg, .pdf, or .txt:

(plot-points df 'x 'y 'output "scatter.png")

The .txt format draws the plot as ASCII art, which is handy in a terminal or over SSH.

docs.title: Facets
docs.text:
Faceting draws one panel per value of a column, like facet_wrap in ggplot2. Pass the column to any plot with the 'facet plot option:

> (plot-histogram flowers 'length 'facet 'species 'facet-columns 1 'binwidth 0.2
                  'xlabel "Sepal length")

Faceting works with layers, too:

> (plot-layers (layer-points flowers 'length 'width 'group 'species)
               (layer-lines fits 'length 'width 'group 'species)
               'facet 'species
               'xlabel "Sepal length" 'ylabel "Sepal width")

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Option Value Default 'facet column name; one panel per unique value, in order of first appearance none 'facet-columns number of columns of panels the smallest number that makes a square or wider grid 'facet-scales 'fixed, 'free, 'free-x, or 'free-y 'fixed

With 'fixed scales, every panel has the same axis ranges, so panels can be compared directly. 'free lets each panel's axes fit its own data. 'free-x and 'free-y free one axis and keep the other fixed. A categorical x axis always has the same categories in every panel.

docs.title: How panels are drawn
docs.text:
• Layers without the facet column are drawn in every panel. For example, a dataframe holding a reference line can be layered over faceted data.
  • Shared across panels: group colors, categorical x positions, and histogram bins all come from the full data.
  • Legend: one legend, to the right of the panels. A 'key string such as "top left" instead places the legend inside the last panel, and #f hides it.
  • Labels: the x and y axis labels are drawn once, centered on the panels. Each panel is titled with its facet value, and 'title goes above all the panels.
  • Ticks: with fixed scales, tick spacing is chosen to suit the panel size. To set it yourself, use 'commands, e.g., 'commands '("set xtics 1").

Note

Panels are drawn with gnuplot's set multiplot. Some 'commands that change the page layout, such as set size or set origin, don't work with facets.

docs.title: Layers
docs.text: plot-layers draws several layers on the same axes, like adding geoms in ggplot2. Each layer can use its own dataframe.

docs.title: (plot-layers layer ... . opts)
docs.text:
draws: each layer in order, so later layers are on top, followed by the plot options.

> (plot-layers (layer-points flowers 'length 'width 'group 'species)
               (layer-lines fits 'length 'width 'group 'species)
               'xlabel "Sepal length" 'ylabel "Sepal width")

Here fits has the two end points of a least-squares line for each species. See examples/examples.ss for how it's computed.

docs.title: (layer-boxplot df x y . opts)
docs.text:
returns: a layer for plot-layers. Each takes the same arguments as the matching plot procedure, but only layer options. Giving a layer a plot option, such as 'title, is an error.

> (define species-means
    (dataframe-aggregate* flowers (species) (avg (length) (mean length))))

> (plot-layers (layer-boxplot flowers 'species 'length)
               (layer-points species-means 'species 'avg
                             'color "black" 'pointtype 9 'pointsize 1.5
                             'label "Mean")
               'ylabel "Sepal length")

docs.title: How layers combine
docs.text:
• Axis labels default to the first layer's columns.
  • Colors: a group value has the same color in every layer, so each species' points and fitted line match above.
  • Legend: each group value appears once, with the first layer's symbol. An ungrouped layer appears only if it has a 'label. The legend title is the group column, if all grouped layers use the same one.
  • Categorical x: if any layer has a categorical x (bars, boxplots, or text values), every layer is placed on the same category positions, in order of first appearance across layers. That's how the means above line up with the boxes.

Note

A histogram has a numeric x axis, so it can't be combined with a categorical layer.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Options follow the columns as name/value pairs. Names are quoted symbols, and values are ordinary expressions:

(plot-lines df 'month 'temp
            'group 'city
            'title (string-append "Temperature in " year)
            'output "temps.png")

An unknown option name, or a name without a value, is an error.

When layering, options are split between layers and the plot: layer options go to a layer-* procedure, and plot options go to plot-layers. The plot-* procedures accept both.

docs.title: Layer options
docs.text:
These describe the data and how it's drawn.

Option Value Default 'group column name; one series per unique value, in its own color and with a legend entry none 'color color; overrides the colors from 'group gnuplot's color sequence 'label legend entry for an ungrouped layer none

Options for specific plot types:

Procedure Option Value Default plot-points, layer-points 'pointsize positive number 1 'pointtype gnuplot point type number 7 (filled circle) plot-lines, layer-lines 'points #t to also draw points #f 'linewidth positive number 2 'pointtype, 'pointsize as for points, when 'points is #t 7, 1 'sort #f to connect rows in data order #t plot-bars, layer-bars 'fill fill density from 0 to 1, or #f for no fill 0.85 'border #t (black), #f, or a color #t 'width total width of the bars at each category, where categories are 1 apart 0.8 plot-histogram, layer-histogram 'bins number of bins Sturges' rule, as in R's hist 'binwidth bin width; overrides 'bins 'fill fill density from 0 to 1, or #f for no fill 0.85, or 0.5 (transparent) when grouped 'border #t (black), #f, or a color #t plot-boxplot, layer-boxplot 'fill fill density from 0 to 1, or #f for no fill 0.5 'border #t (black), #f, or a color #t 'width total width of the boxes at each category 0.6 'pointtype, 'pointsize style of the outlier points 7, 1

To see the available point types, run test in gnuplot.

An option value of the wrong kind, such as 'fill 2 or 'pointtype 1.5, is an error.

docs.title: Fill and border
docs.text:
'fill sets how strongly bars, histogram bars, and boxes are filled with their color: 1 is the full color, and smaller values blend toward the background. When a histogram has groups, the bars overlap, so the fill is transparent instead and overlapping bars show through.

'border draws the outline: #t in black, a color, or #f for none. With 'fill #f 'border #f, nothing is drawn.

> (plot-bars df 'g 'y 'fill #f 'border "dark-red")   ; outlined bars
> (plot-boxplot flowers 'species 'length 'fill 0.2 'border "navy" 'width 0.3)

docs.title: Colors
docs.text: 'color and 'border take a color name such as "black", "gray", or "dark-red", or a hex color "#rrggbb" such as "#b22222". gnuplot has its own list of 111 color names, which doesn't include every CSS name (e.g., "firebrick"); if a name isn't on the list, gnuplot prints an error and the plot isn't drawn. To see the list, run show colornames in gnuplot. Hex colors always work.

docs.title: Plot options
docs.text:
These describe the whole figure.

Option Value Default 'title string none 'xlabel, 'ylabel string the column name ("Count" for a histogram's y) 'key legend position as a gnuplot string, or #f to hide it "outside right top" when there are legend entries, otherwise hidden 'grid #t to draw grid lines #f 'xrange, 'yrange list of two numbers, where #f means autoscale, e.g., '(0 #f) autoscale 'logscale 'x, 'y, or 'xy none 'output file name ending in .png, .svg, .pdf, or .txt (ASCII art) open a window 'size '(width height) in pixels (100 pixels per inch for pdf) gnuplot's default 'commands list of extra gnuplot commands; see gnuplot Scripts '() 'facet column name; one panel per unique value; see Facets none 'facet-columns number of columns of panels about square 'facet-scales 'fixed, 'free, 'free-x, or 'free-y 'fixed

Some useful values for 'key are "top left", "bottom right", "outside right top", "outside bottom center horizontal", and "top left box". Any position accepted by gnuplot's set key works.

> (plot-points df 'x 'y 'group 'trt 'key "bottom right" 'logscale 'y
               'yrange '(1 #f) 'output "scatter.pdf" 'size '(700 500))

docs.title: Plots
docs.text:
Each plot-* procedure draws one layer from a dataframe. Columns are given as symbols, and options follow as name/value pairs:

(plot-points df 'x 'y 'group 'trt 'title "Response")

Each procedure opens a gnuplot window, or writes a file when 'output is given. Its return value is unspecified, unless plot-dry-run is #t.

If x holds strings (or any non-numeric values), it is treated as categorical: values are placed at evenly spaced positions in order of first appearance and labelled on the x axis. plot-bars and plot-boxplot always treat x as categorical.

Missing values ('na) are skipped.

The examples on this page use the data defined in examples/examples.ss.

docs.title: (plot-points df x y . opts)
docs.text:
draws: a scatter plot of column y against column x.

options: 'pointsize (default 1) and 'pointtype (a gnuplot point type number; default 7, a filled circle), plus the options for all plots.

> (plot-points flowers 'length 'width 'group 'species
               'xlabel "Sepal length" 'ylabel "Sepal width")

docs.title: (plot-lines df x y . opts)
docs.text:
draws: a line plot of column y against column x. Rows are sorted by x within each group. A missing y value breaks the line.

options: 'points (#t to also draw points; default #f), 'linewidth (default 2), 'pointtype and 'pointsize (for the points), and 'sort (#f to connect rows in data order; default #t), plus the options for all plots.

> (plot-lines temps 'month 'temp 'group 'city 'points #t
              'title "Average monthly temperature"
              'ylabel "Temperature (°C)" 'key "top left")

docs.title: (plot-bars df x y . opts)
docs.text:
draws: a bar chart with a bar of height y at each value of x. Values of y are plotted as given, like geom_col in ggplot2, not counted. With 'group, the bars for each category are drawn side by side.

options: 'fill (default 0.85), 'border (default #t), and 'width (total width at each category; default 0.8), plus the options for all plots. See Fill and border.

> (plot-bars (dataframe-filter* temps (month) (member month '(1 4 7 10)))
             'month 'temp 'group 'city
             'title "Seasonal temperatures" 'grid #t)

docs.title: (plot-histogram df x . opts)
docs.text:
draws: a histogram of the numeric column x. With 'group, the histograms of each group overlap, with transparent fill, and share the same bins.

options: 'bins (number of bins; default from Sturges' rule, as in R's hist), 'binwidth (overrides 'bins), 'fill, and 'border, plus the options for all plots. The y axis label defaults to "Count".

> (plot-histogram flowers 'length 'group 'species 'binwidth 0.2
                  'xlabel "Sepal length")

docs.title: (plot-boxplot df x y . opts)
docs.text:
draws: a boxplot of column y for each value of column x. Pass #f for x to draw a single box of all y values. With 'group, the boxes for each category are drawn side by side.

options: 'fill (default 0.5), 'border (default #t), 'width (total width at each category; default 0.6), and 'pointtype and 'pointsize (for the outliers), plus the options for all plots. See Fill and border.

> (plot-boxplot flowers 'species 'length 'ylabel "Sepal length")

docs.title: gnuplot Scripts
docs.text: Each plot is sent to gnuplot as a script. These tools let you see that script, and add to it when the options don't cover what you need.

docs.title: plot-dry-run
docs.text:
parameter: when #t, plotting procedures return the gnuplot script as a string instead of running gnuplot. Defaults to #f.

This is a good way to learn gnuplot commands, or to save a script and edit it by hand.

> (parameterize ([plot-dry-run #t])
    (display (plot-points temps 'month 'temp)))
set xlabel 'month'
set ylabel 'temp'
unset key
$d1 << EOD
1 8
2 10
3 13
4 15
1 -5
2 -3
3 3
4 9
EOD
plot $d1 using 1:2 with points pt 7 ps 1 lc 1 notitle

The data are written as inline datablocks ($d1, $d2, …), one for each group of each layer. Missing values are written as NaN, which gnuplot skips. Categorical values are written as their positions on the x axis, with the labels set by set xtics.

To run a saved script:

$ gnuplot --persist plot.gp

docs.title: 'commands
docs.text:
plot option: a list of gnuplot commands, sent after the other settings and just before the plot command, so they can override them.

> (plot-bars df 'country 'gdp
             'commands '("set xtics rotate by 45 right"
                         "set format y '%.0f'"))

Some useful commands:

Command Effect "set xtics rotate by 45 right" rotate x axis labels "set format y '%.1f'" format y axis numbers "set ytics 5" y axis tick every 5 units "set xzeroaxis" draw a line at y = 0 "set label 'peak' at 7, 25" add text at a point "set arrow from 5, 20 to 7, 24" add an arrow "set object rectangle from 3, -5 to 5, 30 fc rgb '#eeeeee' behind" shade a region

See the gnuplot documentation for more.
